title: Budgeting basics
examples: How do I figure out how much money I can actually spend?
What is the difference between a need and a want?
Should I save all my money or spend some of it?

explain.say: Today we are learning about budgeting basics for your money.
Income is any money you receive over a certain time.
Spending is the money you use to buy things you need.
We must always separate our needs from our wants when spending money.

draw.text: Needs vs Wants: Essentials vs Extras

explain.say: A good budget means setting aside a specific amount for saving first.
In real life, you can use a budget to plan for a big purchase.

draw.text: Real Life Example: Buying a bike

faq.q: If I have a lot of money, do I spend it all?
faq.a: No, you should always plan to save some money for the future. Saving helps you reach bigger goals later on.
asks: Should I spend everything I earn?
Is it okay to keep some money aside?

faq.q: Can a want ever become a need?
faq.a: Sometimes, if a want becomes necessary for safety or health, it might change into a need. For example, a warm coat in winter.
asks: Is a phone a need or a want?
When does a want become important?

faq.q: What is the best way to start budgeting?
faq.a: Start by writing down every single source of money you expect to receive. This gives you a clear picture of your total income.
asks: Where do I start my budget?
What is the first step in budgeting?

faq.q: Do I have to keep a budget every single week?
faq.a: It is helpful to check your budget regularly, perhaps every week or two. This keeps you on track with your spending goals.
asks: How often should I check my budget?

faq.q: If I spend all my money on needs, can I still save?
faq.a: It is difficult, but you must always try to allocate a small amount for saving first. This is called paying yourself first.
asks: What if I only have money for needs?
How do I save if I spend everything?

facts: A budget is a plan for your money over a set time.
Needs are things you must have to live, like food and shelter.
Wants are things that improve life but are not necessary, like entertainment.
Saving money means setting aside funds for future use.

quiz.say: If you buy a new video game, are you spending on a need or a want?
quiz.why: Video games are for entertainment, which is a want, not a basic necessity.

wrong.1: It is tempting to think it is a need because you want it very badly.
wrong.2: Income is the money you receive, not what you spend it on.
wrong.3: Saving is what you do with your money, not the category of the purchase.

quiz.say: Which item below is the best example of a basic need?
quiz.why: Food is essential for your body to have energy and stay alive.

wrong.0: This is purely for entertainment and is considered a want.
wrong.2: While shoes are important, a basic need is more about survival than fashion.
wrong.3: This is an activity for fun, making it a want.

quiz.say: If you earn ten pounds, save three pounds, and spend the rest, how much did you spend?
quiz.why: You subtract your savings from your total income: ten minus three equals seven.

wrong.1: This only accounts for the money you decided to save.
wrong.2: This is your total income, not the amount spent.
wrong.3: This is adding the savings back to the spending amount by mistake.
